A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Drama research. Their complete main texts and Appendices A.1–A.8 are readable, and the equations, algorithm, tables, and all ten figures can be matched across versions.

before.justification: v2 reports original Atari100k results, sampling and architecture ablations, grid-world prediction experiments, reconstructed game frames, and timing measurements in Sections 4.1–4.2 and Appendix A.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results in Sections 3.1–3.2 and Appendix A, including Drama evaluations and comparisons of sampling methods and sequence-model architectures.

M1.justification: The Mamba-2 world model, discrete autoencoder, imagination procedure, actor-critic learning, DFS sampling rule, losses, and pseudocode are retained. Renaming 'dynamics model' to 'sequence model' and disclosing additional hyperparameters do not establish a changed method.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same 26 Atari100k games and the same grid-world prediction task. The game subsets used for architecture, model-size, and reconstruction analyses are also retained.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in the Atari tables, DreamerV3XS comparison, DFS-versus-uniform ablation, grid-world experiment, and timing analysis. Mamba-1 is renamed Mamba; the newly cited offline-RL work is not an added evaluated baseline.

E3.justification: The reported evaluation designs retain the 100,000-interaction Atari budget, four-frame skipping, five-episode running averages, model-size comparisons, and grid-world sequence lengths of 208 and 1664. Additional appendix hyperparameters are newly disclosed settings, without an explicit revision to previously stated protocols.

E4.justification: The DFS-versus-uniform ablation has limited revisions to its numerical evidence in Table 4: updated CrazyClimber results place DFS above uniform sampling, and KungFuMaster results narrow its deficit. The ablation questions, experimental designs, and plotted analyses are otherwise retained.

E5.justification: v2's Figure 10 caption identifies the reported intervals as standard deviations; v3 removes that explanation while retaining the same shaded plots. Five-seed Atari reporting and Table 2's mean-plus-standard-deviation convention remain unchanged.

E6.justification: Tables 1, 3, and 4 revise DramaXS/DFS scores from 52,242 to 83,931 for CrazyClimber and from 17,236 to 23,920 for KungFuMaster. Table 1 also revises DreamerV3 scores for those games from 83,931 to 86,225 and from 23,920 to 25,900. Aggregate entries and plotted results remain unchanged; these are limited table revisions, without evidence of new experiments.

T1.justification: The POMDP formulation, SSM derivations, DFS mathematics, and loss equations are retained. Appendix A.6 clarifies the wording of geometric and logical prediction errors while preserving their constraints and averaging rule; no new theorem or proof appears.

C1.justification: Both versions claim a first Mamba-based model-based RL agent, efficient sequence processing, competitive Atari100k performance with a 7-million-parameter world model, and benefits from DFS. The abstract, introduction, and conclusion preserve these contributions and their scope.

C2.justification: v3 explicitly qualifies the DramaXS advantage by naming PrivateEye and Qbert as exceptions in Figure 4. Section 3.2.1 also emphasizes DFS's higher mean alongside a similar median, refining interpretation of existing evidence. The principal long-sequence and visual-reconstruction limitations remain.

D1.justification: Tables 5–7 newly disclose learning rates, weight decay, encoder strides, Mamba dropout, and prediction-head activation and normalization settings. However, Table 5 removes the decoder-filter dimensions. These are documentation changes; the PDFs do not establish corresponding implementation changes.

R1.justification: v3 replaces Ota's Decision Mamba citation with the distinct work by Lv et al. It also acknowledges R2I as prior SSM-based model-based RL, narrowing the previously overbroad research gap to Mamba architectures, and revises R2I's characterization relative to DreamerV3. Most remaining reference changes update bibliographic metadata.

P1.justification: v3 extensively edits prose throughout the main text and appendices, standardizes sequence-model terminology, and renames Mamba-1. It removes v2's duplicated Experiments section, repairs the resulting section structure, expands several captions, and adds acknowledgments.

P2.justification: The document adopts a substantially different conference layout, with changed typography, wider text blocks, running headers, and rescaled and repositioned figures and tables throughout. Hyperparameter-table rows and several captions change, while all ten original figure graphics are retained.

improvement.justification: v3 improves documentation, removes the duplicated Experiments section, and resolves the internally conflicting positioning of prior SSM-based RL. Its revised Drama scores also support the reported 105% normalized mean, whereas v2's displayed scores imply roughly 99%. These limited gains outweigh the loss of decoder-filter details and Figure 10's uncertainty explanation; the underlying method and empirical scope remain stable.
